utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can we deal, then, please, with this agreement, and I'll continue with it. So it's the agreement, I've called out the number and the B/C/S number. Paragraph 1: "All citizens and paramilitary organisations shall surrender all weapons, ammunition and MES regardless of the manner in which they have been obtained by 1200 hours on the 12th of October, 1991, to the military police unit of the 1st" -- it seems to be an interpretation: "Military district." Paragraph 2: "Safe entry to Ilok and searches of all private, public and state-owned buildings in Ilok as locations where weapons, ammunition, and MES have been left, forgotten or hidden shall be made possible. Weapons, ammunition and MES may be retained only by the Ilok police station in the number and quantity corresponding to the inventory list," apparently which was compiled on the 1st of January, 1989. I'll pause for interpretation. "The JNA hereby undertakes the obligation not to inquire about the source and not to sanction the owners in any way, and to conduct the searches strictly according to the Law on Criminal Procedure of SFRY." It would appear, then, that 5, and there seems to be an element of doubt in relation to the translation: "The surrender shall take place on 12" -- with a handwritten correction: "14th October, 1991, at 1200 hours at the location of the 25th of May from the direction of Ilok whereas the searches shall be conducted between the 12th and 15th of October. The JNA units shall secure the occupation of the town and establish the local command which shall ensure peace until the situation has stabilised." And then finally, and I abbreviate, there is the clause that says: "If the use of weapons are endangering the security of the JNA personnel, measures shall be taken pursuant to the decision of the Supreme Command staff on retaliatory measures." And it is apparently signed or authorised. May we ask for that document, please, or those documents relating to the 12th of October to be made an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In relation to this document, I believe there are several problems. The version that I received from my learned friend, as part of today's binder was not signed by anyone from the JNA or anyone representing the authorities of Ilok. The same applies to another copy previously received from my learned friend. This is 00381367, which is the same document, really. Secondly, bearing in mind your ruling and the explanation provided after that objection by my learned friend Mr. Lukic in relation to that military document from Bapska, the previous report, I believe that this document should not be admitted as a separate exhibit. However, if it is admitted as part of the overall report of the ECMM as KII 5 [sic], which is what my learned friend has referred to in this set of questions, then this gives rise to another concern. If we look at the heading of this agreement, this document, we will notice that there is a different reference there, Ky-I-6. I can't help but wonder whether this document belongs to the same set that we have been referring to or whether this document is, in fact, part of a different set of ECMM documents. If so, then it can't be admitted jointly with the previous report, as my learned friend has just suggested. I believe the witness should be in a position to clarify this for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I'm quite happy to ask the witness if he can clarify this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Ambassador, would you -- you've got the agreement in front of you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: At tab 7?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: You have got it, it was -- it's been referred to from the ECMM documentation.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And the date seems to be the 12th of the 10th. Now, can you tell us, please, the source of this particular document that is given the title of "Agreement."

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: As you can read in the report, which was not written by me, but I believe that it was Mr. Waters, or Mr. Finakaliotis. It is definitely not my handwritten. So we were -- there is paragraph 2, we were supplied by both sides a copy of -- and so on. So it was given to us by both sides, and it is not referring to the remark. It is not as a document with signatures. It's a proposal which was given to those people. And we were received it from both sides. According the numbering, it was -- it was -- it is not -- I -- I can't explain it why -- why it is -- the number is another, but it's a part of -- I -- I see it as a part of the document, because it is the document which is mentioned in the handwritten text.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So when you referred to it, are we referring to the document, page number 00381362 at paragraph 2; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: 62, paragraph 2, yes, is that right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I would still, therefore, make application that this bundle of documents at tab 7 be made an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The agreement is, on the evidence of the witness, the document referred to in the ECMM report, which is there referred to as Annex A in paragraph 2 of the report. And, as such, it will be treated on the same basis as the last document that was disputed, which means that it will be received as part of the report. Now, that gives it no greater authenticity than as a document which has been included in the report with this apparent source that is mentioned in the report. It is subject to dispute as to authenticity, which has been made clear by the Defence. And so it's likely to be the subject of further questions or evidence in the future. And, on that basis then, it will be received as part of the bundle of documents which together, for our simple purposes, are tab 7.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: To which we will assign exhibit number 306, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, may we please move on to tab 9? The numbers in relation to this document are ERN 00381369, which is English, and the B/C/S translation should be 03040394. And if that last document can be put on the screens to assist the defendants. Perhaps before moving on to that document, Ambassador, are you able to say whether the agreement that we have just been discussing was a draft agreement or whether it was an agreement that was agreed by both sides, even though the document was not signed?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: No, it was a draft agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And was it used subsequently for the Ilok situation or not?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's move on, then, to the next tab, which is tab 9. It's a handwritten document. It is in English only one page. And the date seems to be the 13th of the 10th --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, has the B/C/S document been shown on the defendants' screens? Could I have some indication from the Defence if that is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You will have to wait a little. There it is. But it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But it's in a form that's not very visible unless it's enlarged.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: May I start? The defendants are able to read the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Not yet, if they have the same display as we have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I can see that Mr. Mrksic is indicating that he cannot read his document on the electronic screen. Well, it seems --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you can proceed now, Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Let's deal, please, with the English version, Ambassador. Where has this document come from, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: It's a normal report of -- of regional centre of Belgrade. It's in the first line of the message. And it is addressed to Zagreb, to our head of mission in Zagreb, to EC Monitoring Mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And the reference is to the Ilok refugees; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: You can see that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, in article 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, let's deal with the two paragraphs, if I may. Could you be kind enough, please, to read out the first paragraph?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yeah, it's difficult to read it, because it is written by

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: "Held meeting with JNA liaison officer this a.m. Mr. Perrin explains our concerns ..." Maybe of: "... refugees in Ilok. Advised liaison officer of referendum today to determine those who wish to leave Ilok."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And is that: "Travel west"?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yeah. "Travel west deeper into Croatia." Paragraph 2: "Liaison officer advised he would contact his higher authority to arrange safe passage west through JNA lines. He stated that not all parts -- not all persons may be allowed to depart. Those suspected of crimes would not be able to. It will be" -- no. "He will try to advise us today and this proposed ROE Cunningham. Note, intend to send team to Ilok today to examine situation and look all villages of extreme interest to JNA."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Are you able to help us with regard to paragraph 1, where there's reference to your concerns about the refugees in Ilok? What were the concerns of the ECMM at that time?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: You already presented the letter we got to mission that people are afraiding [sic] of an attack of JNA, and we are told the same when we were speaking with local inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can we deal with the second paragraph, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Because we have, in the second line: "He stated that not all persons may be allowed to depart. Those suspected of crimes would not be able to." Can you tell us firstly: Was there a position or a stance with regard to the ECMM in respect of people, what I will call refugees, suspected of crimes? Were they in a different category or a similar category, from the ECMM perspective?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can we deal, then, please, with -- we can see clearly that -- "going to send today to Ilok" or "intend to send to Ilok the following day to examine the situation."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, may I please make application for tab 9 to be made an exhibit, both in English and the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number 307.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And then move on to tab 10, because it is the following day. Have you got that, Ambassador?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: The ERN numbers, to assist the registry, are 00381370 and 71, for the English version. And then 72, 73 and 74 are the ones that I've got for the -- well, to assist again the registry, it seems because of the translation difficulties, the numbers -- it's a combination of both English and B/C/S, and it is on the actual index that we have given. It's 00381370, 0038 through to 1374. And then it would appear again there are difficulties with regard to translation ERN numbers, but again on the index that we have given to the registry it should read 03014242, 03014242, and then L004/3502 to L004/3502. But I would like to deal, if I may, please, with the English version. Now, have the -- have the defendants got the B/C/S version in front of them, please? On their screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the defendants have the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's just been clarified that the witness and the accused have the same screens. So that we will have to move to B/C/S on the witness's screen, but as he has the paper document, that is not, I think, a problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do have both documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. If you can please work on paper, we can then keep the B/C/S version for the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I'm going to start with the English version, the defendants have now, I hope, got the B/C/S version. Very well. Let's deal with the English version then, please. The document, it's dated the 14th of October. It's a handwritten document. Tab 10, Ambassador?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Tab 10. 14th of October, 1991. It seems to be that it's coming from Belgrade. And it's going to where, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And the handwriting, if we look just look over the page at 1371, I think it's right to say it's signed by Colonel Cunningham; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Let's deal with, then, please, the first paragraph; there are four in total. Do you know who was actual on this mission or not? You clearly have got Cunningham?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: It was Cunningham and me, as I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you be kind enough, then, please, to read out paragraph 1?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes. "Team spent day in Ilok. After talking to JNA and civic authorities, team attended a meeting chaired by General Arandjelovic, commander of local area. The meeting was conducted in a friendly atmosphere and in good faith. The results are contained in the attached agreement." Point two: "Tomorrow, a team comprised of Mr. Kypr and Cunningham will meet to Ilok to facilitate the evacuation of the Ilok persons who wish to leave - approximately 8.000 at present. The JNA team, Belgrade, will" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: "Provide"?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "... will provide" - I'm not sure about the abbreviation - "... between JNA and Belgrade. Will provide Colonel Memisevic as a liaison officer and Colonel Grahovac, local commander, will be involved in all negotiations/staff planning. In addition, a second team of Waters and Finakaliotis will accompany the original team."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And I think paragraph 3 deals with the concern. Can we deal with that, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes. "The main concern at present is that -- is the agreed departure time/date of 17th of ..." -- I can't read it. "However, this" -- I don't know what does it mean. "Accurate staff planning and personal contacts on the side of all" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Is it "on the ground"?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "On the ground," maybe. "All" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: "Arrangements"?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "Arrangements should be completed on time." I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Let me see if I can assist. "Will attempt to provide all details by 1500 hours tomorrow. And to this end the JNA have indicated that some trucks (possibly 50) could be made available - should know tomorrow." And then 4, what does that say, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: 4: "Both teams plan to spread -- to spend three to four days in Ilok area."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And there is telephone numbers then given?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, can we then deal with the reference to the agreement, "see attached agreement," which is referred to in paragraph 1. If we then turn over -- I will give the references. The English reference I think I have already given, but I will give again is L004/3500 through to 02. And the B/C/S version would appear to be, as I say, 00381372 to 74. Can you assist us? There is one other document which is in B/C/S. I don't know if you've got it in between those two. It is a single document with the number 4242 on it. Do you see that document, top right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Do you know exactly to what that document refers?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: 4242, it's in Serbian. It's the translation of the -- of that Cunningham report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Let's then deal with the agreement. We'll ask for the -- I'll refer to the English, and the B/C/S to be put on the electronic screen. Could I be told, please, when the B/C/S document is on the screen? I seem to think that it's now there. I will abbreviate the first main paragraph, if I may, where it -- if the Court wishes me to read it, I'm quite happy to do so. Your Honour's mic was on and I couldn't help but hear that there was a reference about reading it? I didn't know Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: How anybody can read the B/C/S that was on my screen, I didn't know, but it has now been improved. I was thinking of the three poor accused at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I see. Well, can I deal, then, with the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: The preamble relates to the military command of the JNA, the representation and the authorised representative of the towns of Ilok, Sarengrad and Bapska. Various other individuals. And people who were chairman of the negotiation committee and others concluded the following agreement in Sid on the 14th of October, 1991, in the presence of the European Community mission representatives, Hugh Cunningham, and yourself, Mr. Kypr. Now, can we just confirm, with regard to this document, is it a draft document or was it actually agreed as a guide?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: It was agreed as those two parts. I have to stress that we have no -- we haven't been there, we, as EC monitoring team. We have not been there in the room where the negotiation -- negotiatings [sic] were going on. So we were only told that this is the agreement they -- they agreed upon and that it was signed by those two sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, can I see if I can just clarify this? You are in a building, the ECMM monitors, yourself and Cunningham are in one room; and the other parties are in another room. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: No, it is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, can you tell us then, please.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: There were -- there were two teams from each side, or two groups from each side, means Ilok's authorities and JNA authorities. They went to another room, and the rest of people who were there from the convoy, because we were -- we were providing the security through the way, so we were in the convoy, so we were standing in another room and waiting until they are finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So when did you first see this document, then, please? In what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: When -- when they came out from -- from the other room.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, let's deal with it then, please. Agreement, article 1. I'll read in English. "Based on the request of the citizens of Ilok, Bapska and Sarengrad, and following a referendum," which we have heard about in earlier documents. "All citizens of these towns as well as the refugees currently staying in these towns may depart with their families if they wish." Article 2, and I will abbreviate, if I may, relates to the handover of weapons and explosives, the location being the bridge, and it would be done in the presence of the MUP and the organs from Ilok and the ECMM; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Article 3 relates to the timing, shouldn't be any later than 7.00 in the morning on the 17th of October. Article 4 is a requirement for any operations, or total peace is the phrase used, forbidding any operations and shooting. Article 5. Can we deal with article 5, please? Would you be kind enough to read what that relates to?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: If I can read it from the draft translation. "Upon the departure of citizens from the said towns and before the convoys are formed, JNA members will inspect, search any facilities whose inspection search is deemed necessary in the presence of MUP organs and European Community mission members."

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I hope that this is a good time now that the witness has finished this article. I believe that what my learned friend read out on page 58, line 11 as being article 3 of this agreement, or what he paraphrased as being article 3, is not in reference to any weapons or explosives surrendered. Rather, article 3 says that the Croatian MUP and TO units undertake that they shall immediately remove all the mines and explosives that were laid in the settled areas, and that this should be done by the 17th of October. I think that changes the meaning of the entire paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can we deal, please, with the article 5, there is reference to the European Community mission members. Were you present when this article was adhered to?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: No. We were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: We were not a part of this negotiations. It was not our mandate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So when parties came out from the negotiations and you saw that there were various articles referring to the ECMM mission's participation, did you indicate to them whether you agreed or didn't agree to their proposal?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: We were asked to sign this agreement and we rejected it. So you can't see our signatures there on the paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: But the question I'm asking is: Why did you reject it?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Because we were not a part of that, and we -- we -- our mandate was not to discuss those things. We were there as monitors, as observers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So when we talk about the ECMM mandate, and here we're dealing with Ilok and we will deal with the same mandate when it comes to Vukovar, what was your perceived mandate when you were dealing with such places as Ilok and Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yeah, as you can see from the name of the mission, it's to monitor, to observe cease-fire, the other mandate was to prevent blood-shed if we can help, let's say in communication to hand over messages from one side to another side, if there is no other possibility for contacts of those two sides. But it was more passive than -- than active behaviour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to move on, if I may, to article 10 of this document, which is at page 3502. So it's the very final article. Have you got article 10 there --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: -- Ambassador?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Reading: "Citizens under reasonable suspicion."

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough to read out that particular article, and then I wish to ask you some questions about it.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "Citizens under reasonable suspicion of having committed a criminal offence may not leave the towns or join the convoy. All representatives, that is, members of the National Guards Corps, must leave the above-mentioned towns and join the convoy, unless they have committed a criminal offence. They will be given the same guarantee of their security as the other citizens."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now can I just deal, please, with this reference, because this is not the first time that it has been referred to in your documentation. Here are citizens, the suggestion being that they have committed a criminal offence and they were not to leave the town or to join the convoy. Do you know what actually happened to -- firstly, did you know if any people were not allowed to join the convoy?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: With regard to this article, article 10, I presume you -- you read it at the time; that is correct or not?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: We rejected the -- to sign the -- this agreement because we were not a part of that. So -- so we were not even -- we haven't read that in details. I saw, okay, there is "sporazum," it means agreement, and there are signatures, but nothing more. We got a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So what did you actually do then in Ilok after this?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: In Ilok we helped to -- to prevent blood-shed, so it means to be there on the spot. There were teams sleeping in Ilok. Cunningham was sleeping there to -- to make the village or the city more safe. And I was in the very neighbourhood, and there were other teams. And we asked for support or for help in Zagreb ICRC, because they are the right body to provide such an evacuation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to ask that that particular document or series of documents in tab 10 be made an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number 308.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, that was the 14th of October. If we move then to tab 11, we have got various documents with the following number, 00381376; 77 for English; 78, it would be in French. And then translations in the following number: 03040696, 97, 98, and 88 is the -- 788 is the translation of the earlier document. So could I deal, please, with the document dated the 25th of October? The subject is "Evacuation of Ilok." Have you got that, Ambassador?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: You mean sent by Mr. Perrin?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, that's exactly -- I was going to say firstly, can you see the document, and you can see who signed it. Can we deal, then, please, with the English version, but can we just check the B/C/S version is on the screen? I'm told it is. Let us then deal with paragraph 1, please, which was the document created by Mr. Perrin. Would you be kind enough to read it, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yeah, on the display there is the first page, so we need the second -- yeah. It's there. Okay. From RC Belgrade, Perrin to head of mission Zagreb. "Subject: Evacuation of Ilok." First: "I object most strenuously to the attached article and the insinuations contained therein against two members of my senior staff. For your information, Kypr and Cunningham were on an authorised operation to monitor the cease-fire in Ilok. As is standard practice, and in order to determine the situation, they visited the JNA authorities and then the village senior personnel in Ilok. During the course of the meeting with the senior villagers, the villagers passed on the results of a referendum held the day before. The referendum asked two questions: a - do you wish to lay down your arms; and b - do you wish to leave Ilok? The results were that 940 (it means 26 per cent) wished to give weapons away and 5.347 wished to leave with their children, plus 1.000 from Bapska and a further 1.000 from other local villages. "At the end of the meeting, the village senior personnel asked if Kypr and Cunningham would attend a meeting they had already arranged with General Arandjelovic in the town of Sid at 1200 hours. Kypr and Cunningham explained that they had no knowledge of the meeting and could not attend without agreement of both sides. With the concurrence of both sides, Kypr and Cunningham attended the meeting to observe only. "Contrary to the statement in the attached article, neither Kypr nor Cunningham signed the document. In addition, they did not participate in the preparation of the document which was done behind closed doors, with only the JNA and the village senior personnel present. "In order to preserve and enforce monitor impartiality, on more than one occasion and normally several times a day, the village senior staff was advised in the strongest of terms that Kypr and Cunningham would do whatever the village senior personnel asked them to do in order to continue the cease-fire, prevent blood-shed, and ensure the security of the villagers. The prime and only activity of Kypr and Cunningham was restricted to carrying messages and requests from one side to the other side and back. Also, I must point out that the village had the tacit agreement of Mr. Ivan Juros (head of Ilok in the Senate) who personally told Mr. Petar Cobankovic (village representative who visited Zagreb immediately prior to the evacuation), quote, 'you are there, you know, you do what is best' unquote. Finally, when Mr. Cunningham relayed Zagreb's direct order to the village senior personnel to cease and desist in any activities that could be construed as aiding the evacuation, the presence of the mission is our only guarantee" -- sorry. "The spokesman for the villagers stated quote 'We are totally neutral the presence of the mission is our only guarantee not to be killed -- I don't see an exit for us. We are victims, we can't have control, army can do own work and Ilok may not exist, and Ilok it will be the same as Sarengrad and Bapska.' Unquote. (The statements are somewhat disjointed, as the translator broke down in tears several times, as did several others)."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can I just stop you there? Clearly, then, paragraph 2 relates to Mr. Cunningham taking notes - we'll see that in a moment - and also that there had been complaints by the government of Croatia about your participation in Ilok; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I know it's slightly out of sequence, but I will deal with that, if I may, at this time. But this clearly was a document sent by the ECMM head of mission about the allegations against you?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Is that right? And what were the consequences to you of those allegations?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: According EC Monitoring Mission, none.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And at the end of your ECMM monitoring mission, did you receive any recognition for your part in this procedure?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Maybe after two years I got a silver medal of the ECMM mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was not intending to adduce that as evidence, but clearly it was something that had to be dealt with in relation to Ilok. I would like to move on, if I may, please, I will bypass tab 12, which refers to the details of the referendum, but I will move on to tab 13. It precedes the complaint but is referred to in the complaint. It is the number -- my number is 00381394, 95, 96 are the English version. And then for the B/C/S, it relates to 03040398 and 03041190 is the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, have you got the handwritten document? It's dated the 18th?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: We have heard already the -- I think, the 11th, 13th, the 14th. This is now the 18th. Can we just look at the following page. I think it's signed by Cunningham; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, it's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And I'll deal with the list in due course. Now, with regard to this mission, this again refers to yourself and Colonel Cunningham, visiting various towns?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, reading from paragraph 1, the towns that you visited?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: It was the 16th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Sorry. Yes. The report is the 18th, but the visit was the 16th.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So what towns did you visit, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: We went to Sarengrad, Bapska, Mohovo, Lovas and Opatovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And can you tell us, please, what you found?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: The villages at the end, it means, Lovas and Opatovac were undamaged and appeared normal as stated in this report. All other villages were partly destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And can you please use the report and read from the report in relation to the towns that you referred to?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yeah. "Various homes of the other -- these towns."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: "Three towns"?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "Three towns, especially Lovas, with" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Is that 26?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "... 26 destroyed homes, were damaged, some very severely. The team stopped in Lovas and meet with several local authorities. Of special note concern, the 'chiefs,' chief of the local defence forces - a civilian - spoke to us at great length about the situation in Lovas. His talk could be best described as a rambling" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: "Diatribe"?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "... diatribe covering World War I, World War II, to rambling" -- sorry, "to the present. During his talk, he mentioned plans for the future that involved forced relocation of some 300 to 500 personnel of Croatian extraction ..." I can't read. "Total population of 1.800 of which 136 are Serbs. He also stated that he and other Serbs, volunteers had attacked specific homes in Lovas, the 10th of October, 1991, to prevent Serbs from being slaughtering."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: From being slaughtered, I think.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Slaughtered, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: That's okay.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "During the" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Is that "attack"?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "This attack, 22 Croats and one Serb were killed. The Croats were normal citizens and not Croatian National Guard. The town is consequently being ruin -- run by a council of five of which the chief and the deputy are both Serbs. For your info, Cunningham."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. And then if we turn over, I think it's right to say, at page 1396, we have got a list of individuals, and at page 03041190, the English version, we have got -- it says: "A list of buried civilians killed in the battle to liberate Lovas on the 10th of October."

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, there are 22, as you have described, Croats and one Serb. Did you meet this individual, the chief of the local defence forces; namely, the Serb defence force? Did you actually meet him yourself?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, we have met him, both Cunningham and me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And what was your overall impression of this man? In very short form.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I am not psychologist, but he was -- he looks like he is not very normal person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And there is reference to the plans for forced relocation of some three to 500 personnel of Croatian extraction, or actually of the 1800, 136 were Serbs. What was done in relation to that? Do you know if Croats were relocated?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: No, I don't know, because afterwards I was not in a contact with those villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I please make the documents that are in binder 13, or tab 13 exhibits in relation to this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: These will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number 309.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, I would just like to deal with two photographs. They are at tab 15 and tab 16. And I'll deal with them, if I may. The reference for the photograph at tab 15 seems to be 00381525, 00381526. And with regard to six, and then with regard to the other photograph, it's 1526A. So I would just like to deal with those photographs, if we may. So one is, I will start again, 00381523, 00381524, and then the other one is 00381525, 00381526.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Let's deal with those photographs, if we may. The first photograph should show a tank with two goats in front of it, and an ECMM vehicle. Where was that photograph taken, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I believe that it is Sarengrad. It is written on the -- on the other page of the picture. But it was -- it was written by me afterwards when the pictures were -- were done, so it's maybe 14 days after, and I really can't tell precisely if it is Sarengrad or which, but I -- I presume that it is Sarengrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, in actual fact, I was trying to shorten it, if I could. But if we just turn back a page, you will see the back of the photograph, and we can see that it's Sarengrad, 1524A. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yeah, but -- sorry, sir, but there is a time between when photographs were developed, so maybe my memory in that time was not --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And then can we move on to -- and I will seek to make that an exhibit. If we move to the 1526, we've got a photograph which seems to be a -- an exhumation. Now can you tell us, please, where this is?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, it was an exhumation. We were asked by local citizens from Ilok that -- that there are some bodies buried only for temporary circumstances, and that they wished to have them in the cemetery of Ilok city. So we offered them our service to go to cover the convoy which can -- which can bring those bodies to -- to the City of Ilok.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And were you told how these -- how these people were killed or who killed them?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: We were not -- yes, they were killed, but we were not told by whom, or I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: But were you told whether they were Croat or Serb?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, they were Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to make both these photographs exhibits. So in relation to divider, or number 14, tab 14 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: 00381524 will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number 310.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 311, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I want to deal on -- move on, please, to tab 17. Tab 16 deals with the evacuation itself and perhaps you will be cross-examined on it. Tab 17, which is 00381381, 1382, and then for the B/C/S translation, 03040789 and 90.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And Your Honour, I very much -- I don't know exactly the time, but I would very much like to conclude this document in its entirety, if Your Honour was thinking of a break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, we can stretch on with the tape until --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- 25 to at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Good. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can I deal, then, with this document itself? You've seen it before. In general terms, just looking at it, what exactly is it?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: It is analysis maybe made by the headquarters of ECMM in Zagreb, which established a special team of -- a special humanitarian team which should take care about the developing situation which was getting worse and worse, and there was a lot of those humanitarian problems. And we have to analyse what will be the next future of the mission and what our -- what is happening on the front line on the spot, we are sending there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Let's deal, then, with the very first line. It seems to be in Dutch, the top line. It seems to refer to information. And then it mentions various countries. So what was its distribution, please? To whom did this go?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: This distribution means Coreu. Its distribution within all EU in that time, European community countries.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And what about these other countries that are mentioned which are clearly not in the EU at the time? Top line, please.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, can we just look at it, please.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: We have got -- to me it seems to be Yugoslavian distribution. We've got Stockholm, Ottawa, Prague, Sophia, Budapest.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I cannot comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Very well. Let us then drop a line, then, please. What exactly does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Pres/Hag Coreu?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: In that time it was probably -- I guess "Hag" means Hague, because in that time, as I do remember, the Netherlands was the presidency, the president country of EU.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: About what level of priority did it have?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: It -- it has a priority.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And the date seems to be the 8th of November, 1991, the time being 2205 hours; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: That's the local time. And what was its circulation? Is there any control of the circulation there, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, it is the lowest control of circulation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And it's copies to EC embassies. Now where were these EC embassies?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I don't know what does it mean, because in that time we were not a member of European Union, so I am not aware of this. Where it have been sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, can we deal, then, please, with the subject matter, and would you be kind enough to read out, I'll stop you when we need explanation.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "Subject: 138th report of Monitoring Mission. The following report of violations of the second protocol to the Geneva Conventions was received from HOM on the 7th November, 1991. The monitor mission was investigated complaints of several authorities concerning possible violations of the second protocol to the Geneva Conventions before and during the events of Ilok and the surrounding villages of Bapska, Lovas and Sarengrad. To achieve a balanced investigation, a monitor team was held" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: "Has held"?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "... has held: A, interviews with ECMM members of regional centre, Belgrade: B, interviews with CO headquarters JNA in Ilok: C, interviews with the local friar, Marco Malovic, of the Franciscan monastery of Sveti Ivan Kapistran in Ilok: D, a local reconnaissance of the situation in the villages mentioned before: E, interviews in Rijeka and the surrounding area with the evacuation -- evacuated people."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes, now could you just read a little more slowly because there is a difficulty with translation.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I will try.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's kind of you.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "The search for the truth took four days, 17 hours of hearings and four days of travelling. Two requests to visit Sarengrad or another village were denied. The nearby villages could not be visited for reasons of insecurity and military area of responsibility. "The investigation had of course several limitations: The short time-span available, the limited number of people heard, and the fact that the villages near Ilok could not be visited. "The monitor three -- monitor team, however, has been convinced, after following the above-mentioned approach and cross-checking the received testimonies and the made statements that conclusions can be drawn: In a number of instances there have been violations of the second protocol. "The monitor mission is of the opinion that the JNA frequently, in close cooperation with Chetniks, (called reservists or territorial troops by the JNA) tried to displace as many Croats as possible by creating distraction and/or panic. This view was also supported by a written report from another area. "The JNA scenario have, save the one for Ilok, often involved along the following lines: Tension, confusion and fear is built up by military presence in the vicinity of the villages and by provocative behaviour: Controls, shootings: 2, next there is artillery or mortar shelling for several days. This shelling is mostly aimed at the Croatian part of the village. In this stage, the churches are often hit and destroyed. 3, in nearly all of the cases JNA ultimata are issued demanding the collections and the delivery of all weapons. Village delegations" -- now I am not --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: In actual fact, if you turn over the page, because of the way that the telex was sent, it will only take so many -- so much in. If you look at the next page there is a duplication, and you can see that you were reading paragraph 3, and you can find paragraph 3 repeated.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "In nearly all of the cases" -- thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: That's all right.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "JNA ultimata is issued demanding the collection and delivery of all weapons. Village delegations are formed but their consultations with the military authorities do not lead, with the exception of Ilok, to peaceful arrangement. The practice is strongly discouraging -- discouraged by the Croatian authorities. "With or without waiting for the result -- for the results of the ultimata a military attack is carried out with tanks and/or infantry. 5, at the same time or shortly after the attack Chetniks entered the village to finish the job. Accounts vary then from murder, killing, burning, looting and discrimination. Most of all elderly people who were not able to flee are involved."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can you just do it slowly, please? Thank you. Yes?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "Ilok was not destroyed: As such, it represents an asset with a functional value and serve a showcase to the monitor team. "The systematically denied any guilt referring to the armament of the population and the provocative behaviour from their side. The assumption that the population was armed is mostly true. It appears however that compliance with the ultimatum never changed the further course of events. Attacks with tanks, artillery and armoured infantry against the unarmed or slightly armed villagers. This in itself should be considered a violation of the generally accepted humanitarian principles of proportionality and subsidiarity. "Another defence of the JNA was that they could not be held responsible for the behaviour of the Chetniks. The monitor team is, however, convinced that the JNA very closely cooperated with those reservists and is of the opinion that the leadership of JNA should directly or indirectly be held responsible for their acts. End of text, Hag Coreu."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And that document was compiled on the 8th of November, 10 days before the surrender of Vukovar; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to make the documents in tab 17 exhibits in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number 312.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Moore. That's probably a convenient time then for the break, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: It is. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at five minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. We will be moving on now to the matters around Vukovar. And can I just indicate that the Court, I'm sure, will be equally thrilled to hear that I have additional documents to give you. I am sure you will enjoy enormously. May I just pass these pass these forward? My learned friends have got copies of them. They are Ambassador Kypr's notebook, which I will make application for him to refer to it. That is a handwritten document which I think he has in his handbag. And these are the English and B/C/S translations. So I will endeavour to try and move from the notebook to the witness statement to the file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is it the case that the interpreters have had the benefit of those documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: They have not had the benefit of those documents, as far as I'm aware.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can that be arranged?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I have actually asked for some to be printed. I will just see if there are spare ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Perhaps if I just deal with the preliminary points, and additional copies, I hope, can be -- can be printed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Ambassador, I think it's right to say that you have a notebook, it's the yellow one with the large red patch on the top with the name of "Kypr" on it. Now, that particular document or book, when did you compile the notes within that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: It was used during my mission in -- in those areas in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And when you say "those areas," I think it's right to say that we're dealing with Vukovar; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: The notebook covers -- the first remark is the 18th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes. And I think it's right to say that you would wish to refer to that notebook to assist your memory; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes. If it is possible, I would be very --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I'll seek the Court's leave in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That will be appropriate, Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, to help, I hope, we have prepared an English translation, because the notes within your book which you brought to the ICTY on Monday, they're in B/C/S, Czech and English; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And the -- the notes themselves that we now have typed up were compiled as -- with you sitting down with a language assistant and deciphering what you were saying?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And you have had an opportunity of looking at the typed copy to try and assess its accuracy?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Is that equally correct?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Would you -- perhaps the best way of dealing with it is this way: If we work from the typed copy, I will use with the English, the B/C/S copy can be put on the screen, and you can open your original notebook and just clarify whether it is right or not. Is that possible for you to do?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, may I then just, before we do that, deal with, very quickly, tab 19. Tab 19, I only wish to refer to a short part of this particular document. The English version, which is handwritten, refers to number 00381385, 1386, and the B/C/S version is 03040395, 96 and 97. But I would like to, if I may, please, deal with really the first page, the English page number 1386.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: It's at tab 19, Ambassador.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Excuse me. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And that should be a handwritten document. It states 0 -- if you look at the top left-hand corner of that page, it should start 0815, departure Belgrade; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Excellent. Now, have -- have the defendants got a copy on -- in B/C/S of this document on their screen? I anticipate it will be the number 03040396. I see nods. Good. This again deals with Ilok, and there is only one matter I wish to deal with. It's conversation with a priest. It is the second underlined heading.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: "The priest informed about the following." Have you got that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. "The priest informed about the following: He expected about 800 of the refugees to return within the next week. The JNA had mobilised three bus loads of young men from Ilok." And this is the part: "Of the former 4.000 Catholics in Ilok, only 700 were left." And then: "The JNA is correct about the information on the number of the population." Now, do I read that correctly?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, I do hope.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: The rest of the document merely deals with - when I say "merely," I don't mean that offensively - church artifacts?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would wish to only put document number 00381386 in English and its equivalent translation, which is 03040396. I wish to make that an exhibit, just that part of that page. And that would be the document on tab 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The translation is not only the document ending 96, but also --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I mentioned my concern that the translation may be two pages rather than one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: It is two pages, but the part that I wish to refer to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're having the lot or nothing, Mr. Moore. In fairness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So it's 0396 and 0397. My apologies. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this will be exhibit number 313.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, Ambassador, would you be kind enough, please, to turn to what I will call the Kypr notes.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Because we now move on to the 18th of November. Don't put that file away, because we will be returning to it in due course.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, with regard to these notes, to assist my learned friends' numbering and the Court, this notebook, the handwritten version on ERN is 04687759, 04687792, and the typed version has the same number as indeed the English and the B/C/S. So I wish to refer to the typed version, if I may. My learned friends have got hard copies of it. And now the Court have got the electronic number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And the electronic display will be in B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes, the B/C/S, I hope, will be displayed for the defendants. Could they just let us know when it's arrived?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's there now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I think it's right to say that your first notes relate to a briefing on the 18th of November; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And when you compiled these notes what was the purpose of so doing?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Being a monitor almost each monitor was doing his own notes during our service there, so as have been mentioned in the case of Colonel Cunningham, as well as I was making my remarks to use it afterwards when we were writing reports. Or to use quotations when we were negotiating or referring to this and that point afterwards. So it was -- it was very practical. But the problem is that I was not reading sometimes all sentences. There are abbreviations in English, in Serbian. Sometimes it is -- it was written in English, even though the speaker is Serb, because there was translation. Usually our liaison officers were translating that. So if it seems that the sentence is important for me and I have listened that in Serb, then I wrote it down when -- when he was translating. So it was sometimes -- sometimes it was English, sometimes it was Serb version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, who did you have a briefing with, please, on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yeah. It was General Maksimovic at the 1st Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And was that in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, it is. I hope -- I have no evidence on that. I don't remember, and there is no evidence in the notes

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, I'm just looking at the -- it says the General, and there seems to be a date. And letters BG in the handwritten page?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yeah, it's Belgrade. It's Belgrade, BG is Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And what exactly were you being told by the General, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: We were told first that cease-fire was broken from Croatian side, so because in Vukovar is going genocide. Then it switched to -- to Serbian, the -- so I have to use the translation. "We have an information that by the treatment of the mission they want to prolong resistance in Vukovar."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Just slowly, please. Yes?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "Carry out or bring what they need there. They think to assure their stay in Vukovar or further resistance there through ECMM. We have verified information that they succeeded to infiltrate in Vukovar during the night in order to accomplish the objectives of attack. Last night they operated in certain directions. They did not respect the truce since day before yesterday at 1800 hours. Army -- so army responded in that way." That is in English translation it is missing the "so."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you wait for a minute? There may be a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Could I assist the Court in any way?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: At moment we are trying to get at least the B/C/S version to interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: If it assists the Court, we are having extra copies printed for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can we deal, then, please, had you any way of verifying whether that was right or not, what was being said to you? At that time.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: All the time we were told, so if we are not in the spot we cannot evaluate the information. We are there as a monitor. If we are -- we can monitor only if we are there, and we were not there, so we were told that this is the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, forgive me. I don't understand why the interpreters have not got the same version as the defendants, which would allow them to interpret. That, perhaps, is my misunderstanding, but I thought it was if it was shown on the defendants' screen it would be shown on the interpreters' screen as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Moore. That is correct. Carry on. We're doing what we can to help people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: As soon as the English language arrives, it will be much better.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can we deal, then, please, with your next entry. What does that refer to, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: There is remark: "Adasevci checking point, approximately from 10.15 to 12.22. We were waiting there" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And where is that particular location?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: It's on Serb territory, but we were told by our liaison officer, please, I have to check the situation, please wait. So we were waiting more than one hour, then we decided to turn back to -- for Belgrade. In the very moment we turned back, liaison officers came and that everything is okay and that we can go further.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can we deal, then, please, with your next entry, which I think is at 12.15. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: What language is that in?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: It is written in Czech.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And I think it's right to say that it's been subsequently translated into B/C/S and English. So can you deal, please, with what it was that occurred at 12.15? Use the original if you feel you need it.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I will use the translation, because it should be the same. "Conversation with Dr. Bosanac, 'it was signed at the talks that ECMM" -- it is not correct, so I will follow in Czech original. "It was signed on negotiation that ECMM this morning" -- no, "by this morning." Sorry, it is the end of the sentence. "We visit the Vukovar Hospital by noon. I'm asking you, and she repeated it three times, to come as soon as possible. The situation in the hospital is dramatic. Red Cross couldn't come because they are shooting from the left bank." "They" means JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And what is the next entry, please? Is there a timing at 12.25?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes. We ask for permission in Zagreb to go there to Vukovar, because -- to Vukovar's hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And then I think it's right to say that you had a name or you requested a name to be recorded. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, it is, because it is written by another hand. So I -- I did it when somebody came during the meeting, and I didn't know who is the person, so I asked somebody, our liaison officer or somebody from the other side, to write down the names. So you can see it in my notes few times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Would Your Honours please turn to tab 24, which is an extract from the original notebook, which is 00381411. Go to just tab 24. And for the B/C/S we have got 03040384.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, can we just deal with this extract, we've got it clearly in the middle, Major Veselin Sljivancanin. Now it seems to also have something else written down?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yeah, it is written by my hand, because I was told probably that he is -- he comes from command of Operation Group South Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And where did you get the name from?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I asked somebody on opposite side of the table, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to make that particular extraction from the document at tab 24 an exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number 314.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, if we can just return to the original notebook, please, if you can just close the file for a moment. Thank you very much. And you have the English translation with you as well?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: You've got four documents in total. Can we just deal, then, please with the entry at 12.35?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And what is your entry at 12.35?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Quotation: "Several times we offered them negotiate to give a chance people to leave the cellars." End of quotation. "All our offers were rejected. We stopped the combat operations to make possible a visit for humanitarian operations."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: The reference to, "We stopped the combat operations," are you able to say which area of combat operations were stopped or to which it referred?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on, then, please to the next entry.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: The next entry speaks about 1.300 civilians put out. The next line is hostages, civilians, but it has no other -- other content, and I -- I don't remember what -- what it has meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, can we deal then, please, with the next entry that's referred to.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes. "Representatives of Ustasha forces met one of our commanders at bus station on southeast. It should be finished now."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, before we proceed, "met one of our commanders." Did -- was the name given of the commander that was mentioned on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I am sure not, because I wrote down that one of our commanders, if the name is there, or it should be written there, or there are some points, because I was not able to catch the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can we then deal with your next entry, please.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "Marin Vidic, Bili, called twice by phone. He asked for conditions for help (in the area of city hall)."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And I think it's right to say there was a reference then to proposals; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Made by whom?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. I don't want to guess, so -- it depends on the text and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Let's look at the -- what the proposals are.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "We immediately will stop all combat in Vukovar. He should ask all forces of MUP," means police or Croatian police, "and National Guard to come to the stadium and lay down arms. All." Yes it's visible that it's Yugoslav People's Army proposal. "After that we will provide all facilities for helping. We guarantee full security to all civilians according."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes, now I just want to deal -- we've got the typed version, perhaps it doesn't come through quite as clearly. Can we just go to the original handnote, please, your book?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And the reference to "all," with an exclamation mark?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes. It is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: The "all," is that in a normal writing or is it in enlarged writing?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: It is -- the first is capital, but -- yeah. I use the -- the mark, so it -- it -- it was visible that it is stressed with some -- with some certain importance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, let's then deal with the reference, please.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: There is reference, Vidic. I don't know the sense of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: In English version I got D. Vidic, but the D before, it is illegible, and it is cancelled by me, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, let's read, then, please, what exactly was said.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: There is, in this line, the valid for me is only Vidic, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And the lower, please.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: The lower is: "Prisoners of war from NG and MUP will be changed with our prisoners of war."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes. Can you carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "Main aim and wish is: Vukovar should be free town - all people and citizens could go freely and also our wishes are to save innocent people."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: In the translation we have "and also their wishes." You say "our." Can you just clarify that again?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: It is -- it is written over the previous, and I can see that it is "our wishes."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "Killing and torturing isn't our wish. If they don't accept our conditions, JNA units will be forced to liberate the rest of Vukovar."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Did they explain -- you had had experiences in Ilok and other villages. Did they explain what to liberate Vukovar meant?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can we then carry on, please, with the next entry.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: It means that there are 150 civilians and hostages in cellar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "Six guard were killed, no civilian was hurt. Approximately 15-years-old girl was 15 days ago hit knee by sniper."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And then I think it's right to say, then we look at the typed copy, we've got two inverted triangles?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Which represents a drawing on your -- in your book; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yeah. It is -- there are -- there were two pockets of the -- of the last defence. The left triangle was on the left side, we were told that there are 200 armed people more than 400 civilians in atom shelter, Olajnica, plus hospital. Then we are told that there are in the right triangle, which was around the water-tower, that there are mercenaries, 60 armed people, and unknown number of civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And then I think there was a reference, is there not, to JNA?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I can't explain why is there JNA, and we were told that there are 1.300 civilians, a part of them is in Velepromet waiting to go back to the other parts of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes, and the briefing continued, please.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "20 days before some leaders or chiefs went to hospital and they left maybe towards Vinkovci."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And then turning the page in your original document.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "We stopped all actions now."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, can we just deal your next entry, because that was one location. I think that the next entry appears to be timed at 1445; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: On the 18th?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And that is at Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And why did you go to Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Because in Velepromet it was the place where people, refugees, were gathering.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can I just ask you, please, to look at your original note?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: The previous page. Now, you have your diagram?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And you have the two inverted triangles?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: You have got triangle one, where you have told us on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Triangle two on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Is there a line of what I call English word demarcation running down the page?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
