utterances.text: No, no. There is -- there is a line, but -- but I -- I -- it's a line -- it's an arrow, which shows that this triangle, that the text on the left side is -- is concerned -- concerns the left triangle, if you can see there is an arrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I wonder, perhaps, if we can put this particular diagram, it's difficult to represent it verbally. Can we see that? Yes. Now what I wanted to ask you about, we have got the two inverted triangles?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now you see the left-hand triangle, if you just put your pen to it, please.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: You can see that there is writing that refers to that triangle? Where is that --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, this writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, what is this -- this line --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: It covers all this writing. So it goes from this, there, there is an arrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let's look at what I will call the central part, JNA 1300 civilians. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes. This is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, the JNA, why is there reference to JNA, 1300 civilians in Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, why would you write "JNA"? Would you write that as yourself or would it be as a result of what --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, it is written by me, but I don't know what -- what is the content of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must make an objection. The question by Mr. Moore when he said why is there a reference to 1.300 civilians in Velepromet, this is page 91, line 16 to 17, I don't see any reference to that in these notes. I think -- I don't see "JNA" written anywhere like this, so I think in this way perhaps the Prosecutor was suggesting something to the witness that is not actually mentioned in the notes, at least I don't see that in the notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You see the screen then, Mr. Lukic? Thank you, it's there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And the "Velepromet" is there as well. Maybe the screen is not showing so well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see it on the screen, and I see how it is written in the translation. It's very correctly written in the written translation. In the middle of this sketch it says first "JNA," then it says "1300 civilians," and then below that it says: "A part is in Velepromet." That is what it says. But, with his question, the Prosecutor is suggesting on page 91, line 15 -- excuse me, just one moment. Line 12, three -- "1.300 civilians in Velepromet." The question is on page 91, line 12, that is not what it says in the actual notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's sound, Mr. Moore. It appears to be saying, but the witness will be able to understand his notes better than we can, appears to be saying that a part of 1300 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Is in Velepromet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is in Velepromet.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Let's just clarify, I'm quite happy with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: "JNA" is written by you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Can you then clarify, "1300," does that relate to Velepromet or just part of those people in Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: It is -- it says that a part of them is in Velepromet, As I understand my remarks today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let's just move on, if I may, and leave that particular -- retrieve your notebook, if you would be kind enough, please. Can we deal then, please, with the entry at 14.45?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And the next page, "centrum for refugees." So did you actually attend Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, we -- we were there. I remember that Dr. Schou was there as well. We were speaking there with people, you can see that there is written, not by my hand, the name, of the person, I was told that he is a chief of the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, I wonder if, just to assist the Court, because they haven't got that, can the machine be raised?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes. So, this is the name, and I wrote down by my hand that he is a chief of centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And where did you get that name from?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Somebody has -- has made this remark. It's not my hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, did that -- did that conclude your dealings on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So on the 18th itself, after Velepromet, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: We went to Belgrade to -- but I -- and there used to be usual procedure, but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I wonder if the Court now would be kind enough please to turn over to tab 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I would just like to clarify for the transcript. My learned friend already dealt with the person who is in charge of Velepromet, but we don't have the name of the person anywhere on the transcript. And now that we have the document, it has not been indicated anywhere. The name of the person is Ljubinko Stojanovic. Actually, the whole conversation, without the name, doesn't mean much to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's very helpful, Mr. Vasic, thank you. Yes, Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So I would like, if the Court would be kind enough to turn to divider 21. I will just deal with the ERN numbers, which is 00381398, 1399, 1400. And then the translation is 30938, 39 and 40. That's the typed version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Ambassador, I don't know if it's possible for you to do it, to keep -- well, perhaps if I deal with it this way, because we've got two documents in B/C/S and two documents in English. If we just deal with the -- with the tab 21. If we look at page 1400 we've got "Cunningham," which seems to be the signature at the end; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, this particular document, it refers -- it's from RCB, and its subject matter is, "Negotiations of the evacuation of wounded people from Vukovar Hospital"?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And then there is a date. Now, what date is this, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: It is the 19th, 1400 hours, probably. But I don't know. It's a military style, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, can I see if I can assist you? If you turned to the typed copy of your notes?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And you go to the 19th of November?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And you look at the entry, it should say, I hope, "Negoslavci 1400."

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, it is. In my notes there is the 19th of 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. If we're dealing with it, I'm not trying to lead you but trying to clarify, tab 21 seems to be a document created by Cunningham?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: In relation to the briefing. And the document that you have, the Kypr notebook, is your notes?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's deal firstly with your notes, and then we can deal with other matters subsequently. So dealing with your notes, please. What was the first entry?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: First entry is,"Negoslavci, the 19th of November, Colonel Mrksic, Colonel Pavkovic, operation group south, 1400 hours in Negoslavci. Evacuation of civilians. After yesterday's surrender of Croats, approximately 3.500 people, through night the people were transported." The next point is, "Transported through Lipovac" -- sorry, "Transport through Lipovac was not allowed by Croatian authorities."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And that is a briefing or your -- information that you had?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: It is a briefing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "The people are now in Morovic. Croatian authorities requested to send them between 1500 and 1600 hours near Nustar. It's a short time. We can't do that." Or "it".

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: The next point, "People wanted to go back and there in Ovcara, Negoslavci and other places," means those points in my style of writing. "Will wait new destination." There is written "destiny," but it has no sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: The next point is, "Sweeping mines by JNA on the road through Marinci will be terminated the 20th at 8.00 in the morning."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes, and then turning over, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "A car of ECMM on the beginning and at the end of convoy." The next sentence is, "Protested in the name of SSNO mistreating 2.000 people in Morovic to Zagreb."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Next point, "People from Morovic will go probably" -- it's my interpretation, "to Ovcara".

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Right. I would like to stop, if you would be kind enough, please, and put your original notebook on the highlighter. Now, I want to refer to the reference, "Protested" -- I haven't got that still on my screen. Yes, there we are. So we've got the large exclamation mark. So, "Protested in the name of SSNO." The rest of the notes are in blue. Why was this in red?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Probably to stress the importance of the -- of the message.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And the message being what?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: The message is that in the name of SSNO, which, I believe, it is -- it is Savezni Sekretarijat Za, MOD. MOD. Mistreating 3.000 people in Morovic to Zagreb, it has something to do with the transport that -- the transport from Morovic to Zagreb wasn't able to move, but I -- I don't remember more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And who exactly is the SSNO? What is there function? You said that you're dealings with the Balkans?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: It was told that it is that those on the other side of the -- of the table, probably the -- the Colonel Pavkovic or Colonel Mrksic were protesting in the name of SSNO. Because there was no -- as I remember, there was no civil persons to -- which used to be from the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So you think it was Colonel Mrksic or Colonel Pavkovic who were protesting?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Or somebody -- somebody from the other side, from the side of JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we just take your notes back, please? Now, what is -- we've already dealt with Morovic to Ovcara. Can we deal, please, with the next entry, which should, I hope, deal with radio intercepts that allegedly have been made.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yeah. "Radio intercepts. We intend to get representatives in the Vukovar Hospital and in that way to ensure that nobody is taken out of there."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And what did you understand that meant?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: It means that we were told that it was intercepted by JNA, by the JNA, nothing more. I have no other information, because ECMM has no interception.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Possibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Of course. But: "We intend to representatives in the Vukovar Hospital, and in that way to ensure that nobody is taken out of there." What did you think that meant that caused you to write it down?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I believe that they wish to ensure the situation in Vukovar's hospital as it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And who is "they"?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's deal with the next, please. The next entry.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: The next entry, it's an information that there are 600 to 800 wounded, 300 of them badly. I can't read it now. Yes, lying. "We have no any guarantee of their care in Zidine." It relates to the crossing point because they, it means those wounded people, had to be hand over to Croatian hands in Zidine, probably. It's the sense of this sentence. "We provide enough vehicles and also medical staff, which will take care of the mission."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Enough number of ambulances, certain number of buses for slightly wounded. Medical groups of JNA will go to the hospital. Vehicles will come to Negoslavci the 20th of November at 700 hours with escort of military police, and they will move to hospital. "Driving will go from Vukovar to Bogdanovci, Marinci, Zidine."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And that was the route that was being proposed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, yes. "Our engineers are cleaning road." There is down on the page remark "hostages" but I can't refer to what.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, can we deal with any timings that were given, please, for the 20th?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: For the 20th, on the next page, there is 7.30 will start loading of wounded people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And the wounded of people from where?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I don't know. It should be wounded people are aware, as we were informed only in Vukovar, but I have no information there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: So when there was reference to Vukovar Hospital, was that a separate consideration for you?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: No. No, it -- it is Vukovar Hospital, but it is not -- there is no mention Vukovar Hospital, so you ask me from where, so it is not mentioned there. I wish to be as precise as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes, well thanks for that. And then what was the next timing you had, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And where was that entry?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: It was on the same spot, probably. "Serbs, Territorial Defence" -- sorry, I will use probably, this -- this part of translation. Okay. I will translate it by my own, but please use the official translation there. "Serbs, Territorial Defence, volunteers, will not allow us -- will not allow that convoy can pass through -- can go if there is in it will be even only one single Croatian soldier. If people knew that in the convoy are Ustashas, they will liquidise all in the convoy as well as us and you. And there is no one agreement which can resolve that."

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Now, who was telling you that the volunteers would not allow the convoy to pass through, and indeed if there was a single Croatian soldier/Ustasha on it?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I don't remember. It was somebody from JNA side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, let's see if we can try and remember where you are when this was being said to you. Now, who was telling you this? Was it military or was it civilian?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: No, military. There were on the other side from the side of JNA, there were only -- only military persons. I don't remember that there are some civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes. And can you remember where you were when this was said to you? We know that you were around the Vukovar area, but were you in Vukovar? Can you please try and paint a picture for the Court?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: It was some small house, I believe, but I can't remember more. I know that I was sitting and behind me there were doors, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: But I -- I have no other ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: You have told us that it was JNA. Have you any idea of the sort of rank of the person or number of persons who were there?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. Let us --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: But there were even other monitors, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm just asking about you, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right. You've told us, then, about liquidate. Let's carry on, then, please.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: "As concerns us, we can fully respect the point, but we can't guarantee that they will -- that they -- you and no one single wounded can go -- can leave -- can abandon Vukovar if there is own -- even only one" -- there is no full stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, just to help everybody, you of course had this document in the original form. You were asked to go through it with a language assistant for an interpretation, perhaps less stressful circumstances?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: And we have the document, the typed document for that translation. Would it assist you to --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: -- stick to the --

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: The typed document? The interpretation that I have is -- could you just listen for a moment, Ambassador, please?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, I am listening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That as for us, we can fully respect this point, so we cannot guarantee to you or any wounded person to leave Vukovar if there is only one there. Does that correspond?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. "If there is only one there," to what is that being referred? Well, you have it your notes, I think, don't you?

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: It's only one -- it can be the same as -- as in previous, because --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: PETR KYPR
utterances.text: As in previous statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's just move on, please. What is the next entry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Moore, I'm sorry, but we've reached well over time and virtually the end of the tape. We must, I'm afraid now, adjourn and resume on Monday at 2.15. Sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 27th day of March, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.
